text:
maria-ps: Customer reported a sudden spike in 401s from their private VPC after last night's cert rotation. They say SDK calls started failing for some hostnames but curl from other hosts works fine.
alex-run: Can you paste the error from the SDK logs? 401s usually mean auth but cert issues can cause TLS handshake failures that manifest weirdly.
maria-ps: Here's the error snippet from their Node SDK agent (redacted):

```
Error: request failed with status code 401
at IncomingMessage.<anonymous> (node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:...)
caused_by: TLS handshake failed: "certificate verify failed"
```

jamie-sre: Ah, their proxy is returning a 401 after failing client TLS verify or after mutual auth failed? Do we have an s_client trace from their app host?
maria-ps: Requested it — attaching output from openssl s_client -connect api.customer.internal:443 -showcerts -servername api.customer.internal run from their app pod:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = OldCA, CN = Old Root
verify error:num=27:certificate not trusted
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...old root...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...new intermediate cross-signed...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...leaf...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

jamie-sre: That chain ordering looks like leaf -> cross-signed intermediate -> old root, but clients expect full chain with current intermediate and root first. Could be our rotator uploaded a bundle with intermediates in the wrong order to their private ELB/proxy.
support-ian: Also ask if they have pinned truststore or certificate fingerprint checks in their SDK. Cross-signed intermediates can cause validation to pick the wrong chain and pick an expired/old root, even if the leaf is valid.
alex-run: Two quick repro checks for them: (1) curl --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt https://api.customer.internal:443 -v and (2) openssl s_client -connect api.customer.internal:443 -showcerts -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt -servername api.customer.internal. If curl shows "SSL: certificate verification failed" but s_client shows chain with verify error, it's chain order or missing intermediate.
maria-ps: They ran the curl check. Output: "SSL: certificate signature failure" from some app hosts, but other app hosts (in same VPC) succeed. Looks like an intermediate cached in their sidecar proxy on some nodes.
jamie-sre: That explains the host-to-host variance. Common causes: (a) rotator uploaded new bundle but proxy pods didn't reload and are serving old cache mixed with new chain; (b) HAProxy/Nginx instance concatenated certs in wrong order on reload; (c) client-side pinned cache. Steps to resolve: force-reload proxy on affected nodes, ensure bundle order is leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root, and confirm OCSP stapling can reach responder if stapling enabled.
maria-ps: They confirmed they use our Private rotator which uploads PEM bundle to their ALB sidecars. Their ops ran a restart on the sidecar and the node became healthy. Still one node continues failing.
alex-run: Tell ops to check the file on the node: /etc/rotator/certs/api.customer.internal.pem and run:

```
awk '/BEGIN CERT/{i++} {print > ("cert" i ".pem")}' api.customer.internal.pem
openssl x509 -noout -text -in cert1.pem | grep "Subject\|Issuer\|Not After"
```

support-ian: Also check for extra trailing newline or garbage at EOF. We saw cases where an extra "\n" after PEM caused haproxy to ignore the intermediate and only serve leaf+root in the wrong order.
maria-ps: Ops ran that and found two intermediate certs present; one is the legacy intermediate (cross-signed) and the new intermediate. File ordering was: leaf, legacy-intermediate, new-intermediate, root. They swapped to leaf, new-intermediate, legacy-intermediate, root and reloaded sidecar — affected node immediately started passing SDK requests.
jamie-sre: Nice. Also recommend they pin the rotator to upload order-checked bundles: add a validation step that checks chain with openssl verify after upload:

```
openssl verify -CAfile /path/to/root.pem -untrusted /path/to/intermediates.pem /path/to/leaf.pem
```

alex-run: For long-term: add a post-rotation hook that restarts edge proxies in the VPC and clears any in-memory cert caches (haproxy shm, nginx ssl_session_cache). For HAProxy:

```
echo 'show ssl cert' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy.sock
# and after reload
kill -USR1 $(cat /var/run/haproxy.pid)
```

maria-ps: Customer ops also raised a question about OCSP egress — they have strict egress allowlist. Does OCSP stapling failing cause this symptom?

jamie-sre: If stapling is required and OCSP can't be reached, some setups will serve an incomplete chain or fail at handshake. But more often stapling failure leads to slower handshakes or stapling absent, not immediate 401. Still, verify egress to OCSP and AIA URLs from the edge nodes.
support-ian: Closing notes to customer: (1) fixed by reordering bundle and reloading proxies on affected nodes, (2) we recommend adding chain verification in rotator, (3) add post-rotation proxy restarts/clear cache, (4) ensure allowlist includes OCSP/AIA hosts and that clients don't pin old CA fingerprints. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Deployment 2026.03.17-rotator-bundle-validate rolled out to staging (tests: chain-order-check, proxy-reload-hook).
